tickets.title: Third Avenue L stop closure pilot
tickets.summary: A public speaker who built a simulation from MTA trip data argued that closing the Third Avenue L stop would save riders significant time, because only about 5% of people board or alight there. He noted the stop is not a transfer station and is not wheelchair accessible. Action: Refer the proposal to the transportation committee and ask the MTA about piloting closure of the stop.

tickets.title: 11th Street bike storage and delivery worker congestion
tickets.requester: Keith Powers (State Assembly Member); Susan Cestor (District Manager); public speakers (unnamed)
tickets.summary: Over a hundred electric delivery bikes are stored overnight on the sidewalks and street at 11th Street, obstructing the block, pushing businesses out, and raising fire concerns. Delivery workers have no legal parking or corral space, and the district office has worked on the issue since February 2024. The 9th Precinct plans enforcement on October 7 that could confiscate bikes, and speakers asked for notice and multilingual outreach to workers. Action: Follow up with the precinct and agencies on a compassionate enforcement approach, multilingual notice to workers, and sites for bike parking.

tickets.title: Drug activity and lighting in Seward Park
tickets.requester: Susan Cestor (District Manager); Parks committee chair (unnamed)
tickets.summary: Residents and park users report increased drug use and homelessness in Seward Park, and the Lower East Side Ecology Center is affected by drug use at a nearby bathroom. Dark spots and out lights in the park may enable drug use, and a speaker asked whether mobile crisis teams could respond instead of police. A police task force is already active in the park, and the district office gets weekly needle collection reports. Action: Follow up with the precinct and Parks on drug activity and lighting, and ask residents to report out lights through 311.

tickets.title: Allen Street full liquor license application
tickets.summary: The board voted 20 to 10 with nine abstentions to recommend outright denial of a full liquor license for a new location at 11 Allen Street, an operator tied to a problematic nearby prior location. The committee had earlier favored approval with stipulations, and the State Liquor Authority can still approve without them if the board does not attend. Community opposition at the meeting was limited. Action: Organize community members to attend the SLA hearing and support the denial recommendation.

tickets.title: August SLA resolution wording corrections
tickets.summary: Two August SLA resolutions contained wording errors that described full on-premises denials, when the applications were for beer and wine licenses. Item ten was Soft Hours Tea House and item three was Cozy Cafe. Action: Staff to correct the resolution text for items three and ten to read beer and wine license.

tickets.title: Essex Market RFP postponement and community role
tickets.summary: The land use and economic development committees passed resolutions asking EDC to shape the Essex Market RFP so the market stays community-oriented. EDC was not prepared to say whether those resolutions were incorporated, and the RFP was due to go out by the end of the month. Action: Meet with EDC this week to clarify how the resolutions are reflected and ask EDC to postpone issuing the RFP.

tickets.title: Free public restroom pilot locations
tickets.requester: Oie (Mayor's Office); Arnett Scott (Transportation committee chair)
tickets.summary: The city is installing 17 free public restrooms citywide as a one-year pilot, with two in the district, including one near Delansancy Plaza and one at Cooper Square and East Sixth Street. Access, emergency calls, and upkeep by a contractor raised concerns. Action: Board to vote next month on a resolution setting out access and emergency procedures during the pilot, and the Mayor's Office asked for suggestions of community sites.

tickets.title: Transportation equity analysis with IBO
tickets.summary: The transportation committee met with the Independent Budget Office to assess whether the district is getting its fair share of transportation resources compared with other districts. Ideas were narrowed to about three, including cross-town buses and neighborhood parking locations. Action: IBO to research the shortlisted transportation equity ideas and report back to the committee.

tickets.title: Manhattan Bridge exits and Canal Street redesign update
tickets.summary: The transportation committee sent a letter to the mayor and DOT reiterating community concerns at the foot of the Manhattan Bridge exits, especially after a recent fatal crash. The letter also requested an update on the Canal Street redesign, since the district has had no update since January. Action: DOT and the Mayor's Office to respond to the letter and provide the Canal Street redesign update.

tickets.title: Congestion pricing impact on FDR Drive
tickets.summary: A board member noted that the earlier air quality report on congestion pricing projected increased congestion on the FDR, which the board had addressed in a prior resolution. The member asked whether that impact actually occurred and whether reporting is planned. Action: Ask MTA or DOT whether they will report on FDR congestion impacts, and request that reporting if it is not planned.

tickets.title: Mobile voting option for CEC elections
tickets.requester: Health and Human Services committee chair (unnamed)
tickets.summary: Turnout in Community Education Council elections has been about 2%, partly because many households rely only on smartphones and some parents are not signed into the NYC schools account. The proposed resolution supports piloting a mobile-first voting option that keeps in-person voting, with multilingual outreach and clear eligibility messaging. Speakers also raised concerns that immigrant families may fear data collection. Action: Vote on the resolution and send it to the DOE urging a mobile voting pilot and expanded parent outreach.

tickets.title: Board trainings on SLA, Robert's Rules, and office procedures
tickets.summary: The board chair announced planned trainings on SLA, Robert's Rules, and office procedures, mainly for new members and as a refresher for others. Dates have not yet been set. Action: Report training dates to the board, and members should email the chair with training topics or questions.

tickets.title: October district needs and budget priorities vote
tickets.summary: The board will vote in October on its district needs statement and ranked expense and capital budget priorities for each city agency. Committees develop the priorities throughout the year, and district managers meet with agencies in September and early October to learn about cuts and vacancies. Summer youth employment was given as an example of a program needing more funding. Action: Committees to rank agency expense and capital priorities for the October vote.

tickets.title: Draft housing plan comments on affordable units
tickets.summary: The city's draft housing plan proposes about 7,000 units over five years, but 75% are market rate, while the board's top need is affordable housing. The board had only a short turnaround to comment, so comments were based on prior positions. Committees were urged to take positions on such plans proactively. Action: None; the board already submitted comments on the draft housing plan.

tickets.title: Bylaws attendance procedure revisions
tickets.summary: Proposed bylaw changes would handle excessive absences earlier, with a letter and a meeting with the executive committee after the first problem, instead of waiting for a removal process. Removal for attendance would be taken out of the main removal process, and public members would have to follow conflict of interest policies. Members raised a concern about the double recommendation step. Action: Vote on the bylaws changes at the October full board, after the 28-day notice is emailed.

tickets.title: Second vice chair election result
tickets.summary: Daniel Tano and Zachary Thomas ran for second vice chair, and the board voted by ballot. Daniel Tano received 25 votes and Zachary Thomas received 14. Action: None; the board elected Daniel Tano as second vice chair.

tickets.title: Transit fare support for uptown immigrant center
tickets.summary: A speaker asked whether MetroCards or OMNY support will be offered to immigrants who need to travel to the new Manhattan Immigrant Welcome Center on 125th Street, which can take an hour by subway with multiple transfers. The speaker noted the trip is hard for Harlem residents without fare help. Action: Elected official liaison to raise the transit fare support question with the relevant office.

tickets.title: NYCHA residents seeking food and necessities
tickets.summary: A speaker from NYCHA housing said residents in poverty lack food, water, and other necessities and need work and communication access. The speaker also raised drugs and toxicity in the community. Action: Refer residents to district office social services contacts for food and necessity access.

tickets.title: Roller skating rink proposal on East River Pier
tickets.location_raw: East River Pier across from the Katherine Slip Mall
tickets.summary: A speaker proposed a 300,000 square foot multi-use indoor roller skating facility on the East River Pier to replace closed rinks, with admission set at $8 and projected jobs of 250 to 400. The speaker described the site as between the Manhattan and Brooklyn bridges. Action: Refer the pier proposal to the land use committee for review.
